title: Uniform linear factorization after adic precision loss for power-split differentials
statement: Let $R_0$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $K_0\subseteq R_0$ an ideal, and $c\geq0$. For a commutative ring $R$ and ideal $K$, write $\operatorname{gr}_K(R)=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}K^j/K^{j+1}$ with its graded multiplication [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then there exist integers $e\geq0$ and $N\geq2e+1$ such that the following holds for every Noetherian commutative ring $R$, ideal $K\subseteq R$, and degree-preserving unital ring isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}_K(R)\cong\operatorname{gr}_{K_0}(R_0)$. For any $n\geq N$, put $R_n=R/K^n$ and $s=n-e$. Let $M$ be a finite $R_n$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $r\geq0$, and $d:M\to R_n^{\oplus r}$ an $R_n$-linear map. Suppose that for every $a\in K^c$ there is an $R_n$-linear map $h_a:R_n^{\oplus r}\to M$ with $h_a d=\bar a\operatorname{id}_M$, where $\bar a$ is the image of $a$ in $R_n$. For every $R_n$-linear map $u:M\to K^n/K^{2n}$ there is an $R_n$-linear map $v:R_n^{\oplus r}\to K^s/K^{2s}$ with $v d=\rho u$, where $\rho:K^n/K^{2n}\to K^s/K^{2s}$ sends the class of $x\in K^n$ to its class modulo $K^{2s}$. Both quotient modules have the $R_n$-action induced by multiplication in $R$; in particular $K^nK^s\subseteq K^{2s}$ since $s\leq n$. No completeness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GAC (lemma-factor-hom), with e=(d(S)+2)c and a larger threshold; factor multiplication on M through d and compose the displayed finite sum of Hom maps with the maps h_a. Tag 0GA6 (section-uniform), invariance of d(S), q(S) under graded ring isomorphism. This module formulation avoids the ill-typed Ext subscript in Tag 0GAD (lemma-bound-two-term-complex), discussed in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-graded-near-projective-hom-divisibility] to $(R_0,K_0)$ to obtain $D,q$. Set $e=(D+2)c$ and $N=\max(q+e,2e+1)$. These constants are independent of $R,K,M,d,u$. For $n\geq N$, we have $n\geq c$, $n\geq q+(D+1)c$, $n\geq(D+2)c$, and when $D=0$ also $n\geq q+2c$. Thus every numerical hypothesis of the cited result holds, including its separate zero-dimensional threshold.

proof.text: For every $a\in K^c$, use $f_a=d$, $g_a=h_a$, and $r_a=r$ in the cited lemma's factorization hypothesis: $g_af_a=h_ad=\bar a\operatorname{id}_M$. The finite generating set of $M$ over $R_n$ also generates it over $R$, since every coefficient in $R_n$ lifts to $R$. Thus this is precisely the finite near-projective module condition, with no injectivity assumption on $d$.

proof.text: Put $t=n-(D+1)c$ and $s=n-e$, so $t=s+c$. By [lem-per-graded-near-projective-hom-divisibility], there are finitely many $a_j\in K^c$ and $R_n$-linear maps $\psi_j:M\to K^s/K^{n+s}$ such that $pu=\sum_j\mu_{a_j}\psi_j$ in $K^t/K^{n+t}$. Define $V=\sum_j\psi_j h_{a_j}:R_n^{\oplus r}\to K^s/K^{n+s}$. Then $Vd=\sum_j\bar a_j\psi_j$ in $K^s/K^{n+s}$, by linearity and $h_{a_j}d=\bar a_j\operatorname{id}_M$.

proof.text: The inclusions $K^t\subseteq K^s$ and $K^{n+t}\subseteq K^{n+s}$ define $\lambda:K^t/K^{n+t}\to K^s/K^{n+s}$. On representatives, $\lambda\mu_a(y)=ay\bmod K^{n+s}$ and $\lambda p(x)=x\bmod K^{n+s}$. Hence $Vd=\lambda pu$. Since $s\leq n$, reduction defines $\beta:K^s/K^{n+s}\to K^s/K^{2s}$; set $v=\beta V$. On every $x\in K^n$, $\beta\lambda p(x)=x\bmod K^{2s}=\rho(x)$, so $vd=\rho u$. Each map respects multiplication by $R$ and therefore by $R_n$: $K^nK^s=K^{n+s}$, which is zero in the intermediate quotient and contained in $K^{2s}$ in the final one. This constructs the required $v$ without completing $R$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_graded_power_split_linear_factorization (R₀ : Type u₀) [CommRing R₀] [IsNoetherianRing R₀] (K₀ : Ideal R₀) (c : ℕ) : ∃ e N : ℕ, 2 * e + 1 ≤ N ∧ ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (K : Ideal R) (E : associatedGraded K ≃+* associatedGraded K₀), (∀ j : ℕ, E '' Set.range (DirectSum.of (associatedGradedPiece K) j) = Set.range (DirectSum.of (associatedGradedPiece K₀) j)) → ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{v} (R ⧸ K ^ n)) [Module.Finite (R ⧸ K ^ n) M] (r : ℕ) (d : M →ₗ[R ⧸ K ^ n] (Fin r → R ⧸ K ^ n)), (∀ a : (K ^ c : Ideal R), ∃ h : (Fin r → R ⧸ K ^ n) →ₗ[R ⧸ K ^ n] M, h.comp d = Ideal.Quotient.mk (K ^ n) (a : R) • LinearMap.id) → ∀ u : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk (K ^ n))).obj M →ₗ[R] (K ^ n).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (K ^ (2 * n))), ∃ v : (Fin r → R ⧸ K ^ n) →ₗ[R] (K ^ (n - e)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (K ^ (2 * (n - e)))), ∀ (x : M) (y : R), Ideal.Quotient.mk (K ^ (2 * n)) y = (u x).val → Ideal.Quotient.mk (K ^ (2 * (n - e))) y = (v (d x)).val
